key_provisions_or_claims: Calls for a common human-centric, risk-based EU regulatory framework for AI based on Article 114 TFEU
Calls for mandatory disclosure when consumers interact with AI systems
Urges updating the General Product Safety Directive and Product Liability Directive, including possibly reversing burden of proof, covering AI and robotics products
Liability in all AI applications should always lie with a natural or legal person
Supports regulatory sandboxes, standardisation, voluntary trustworthy label and cybersecurity-by-design requirements
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament resolution of 20 May 2021 on removing digital single market barriers and improving AI use for consumers. It calls for a human-centric, risk-based EU AI framework, mandatory AI interaction disclosure, updated product safety and liability rules covering AI and robotics, standards, sandboxes and cybersecurity. Embodied AI appears only in transport and agriculture passages.
